title: Quiet Express: Cabin 909 Demo Brings a 7-Day Train Time Loop to Steam
excerpt: STUDIO909 released a 30-minute Steam demo for Quiet Express: Cabin 909, a Blue Prince and Road 96 inspired mystery with a seven-day time loop.
content:
If you loved Blue Prince or Road 96, this demo is made for you. STUDIO909 released a Steam demo for Quiet Express: Cabin 909 on Friday, October 16, 2026. It takes about 30 minutes to finish, so it’s an easy way to test the idea.

If you want fast action or big open worlds, you can skip this one. It’s a slow, puzzle-heavy mystery about talking to people and opening doors.

What Quiet Express: Cabin 909 Is About

You spend seven days on a train, travelling from one side of a continent to the other. Your goal is to find Cabin 909. According to the press release, the passengers and even the conductor say no cabin with that number exists.

Then the train goes up in flames before it reaches the last station. Everyone on board dies. You wake up at the start, with time rewound by seven days.

The loop keeps repeating. Each run, you get closer to why it happens and what Cabin 909 really is.

The studio describes it as a mystery adventure inspired by Blue Prince and Road 96. The press release came from Automaton PR.

Cabins That Rearrange Like Puzzle Pieces

The Blue Prince comparison comes from the cabin system. You wake up in the rearmost cabin and work your way to the front. Each time you open a door, you may find a different cabin.

You get three choices for what’s behind it. Exploring can unlock a different selection, or an extra choice, on later doors. There are passenger, restaurant and storage cabins, among others.

All the cabins connect to each other. Change how they join up, and you may reach new places and learn more about the train. The release also teases small oddities: a locked door, a switch that does nothing, and a space above the ceiling.

Passengers With Their Own Problems

The Road 96 side comes from the people you meet. Every time the train stops, new passengers join. Some are half-human beasts, some are giants, and some are homunculi.

According to the release, the age of discrimination is over for them, and they ride together as equals. Each one brings a story, a destination and a worry. If you talk to them and help out, you may change their journey. You may also change your own.

That’s the pitch. Talk to people, solve their problems, and inch closer to the cabin that shouldn’t exist.

What You Can Do in the 30-Minute Demo

The demo is built around the day-seven disaster. STUDIO909 says it offers multiple ways to prevent the derailment. So you’re not just watching the loop. You’re trying to break it.

The studio revealed the demo at The MIX Fall Showcase 2026 alongside a new trailer. Here it is:

The studio also opened an official Discord server for the game. It says players can find gameplay tips and updates on the demo there. It’s a handy place to compare notes if you get stuck on the loop.

Who Made It and When the Full Game Arrives

STUDIO909 is a Tokyo-based studio set up to make this game. It’s led by director Kazuhide Oka, who is known for Natsu no Kanata and Girls Made Pudding. The release calls him a story writer and indie developer.

Steam lists the full game for 2027 on Windows. It’s a single-player game, and the release lists Japanese, English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Korean. The price hasn’t been announced.

The Steam page is at https://store.steampowered.com/app/3962240 if you want to wishlist it or grab the demo. Players who like mystery loops and don’t mind slow pacing should get a clear sense of the game within half an hour.
